# Extraction

As suggested by the assignment, we decided to extract our corpus from the [Project Gutenberg](https://www.gutenberg.org/). We first selected the authors we wanted to work with, three realists (Balzac, Flaubert and Zola) and three romantics (Dumas, Sand, Sue). We then selected ten books for each author among the ones available on Project Gutenberg. They are the following:

```{python}
#| label: books-table

from pyspark.sql import Window
from IPython.display import Markdown

win = Window.partitionBy("author").orderBy("title")

Markdown(
    books
    .select("author", "title")
    .distinct()
    .withColumn("rank", F.rank().over(win))
    .groupBy("rank")
    .pivot("author")
    .agg(F.coalesce(F.first("title"), F.lit("")))
    .drop("rank")
    .toPandas()
    .to_markdown(index=False)
)
```

*Note: Project Gutenberg only have 8 books from Flaubert so to make the comparison fair, we also selected 8 books for Sue. That way, we have a balanced dataset between realists and romantics.*

Each of these books is identified by a unique ID on Project Gutenberg. All the information about the books (title, author, type and ID) is stored in a CSV file that we created ourselves. We then read this CSV file with Spark and download the books in parallel using a UDF. The downloading process itself is done using the `gutenbergpy` library, which provides a convenient way to access the books on Project Gutenberg. We used the `get_text_by_id` function to download the raw text of each book.
